Hi Oliver / FinLytics team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and helpful context on the product traffic shape. I promised to summarize the open items we need to size a Dedicated capacity proposal and call out next steps. Attached is a very short capacity worksheet (finlytics_capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx) you can fill in where helpful.

Key asks / items to confirm:
- Target traffic profile: sustained RPS/TPS, peak burst duration, and peak TPS numbers (we have a rough note of 30 req/s sustained and short bursts up to 120 req/s — please confirm).
- Token mix: median input tokens, median output tokens, and 95th percentile token count per call (helps with KV cache & memory planning).
- Latency SLO: 95th and 99th targets (you mentioned ~300ms 95th as a goal).
- Model family & size: do you expect to use an open quantized Llama-family model, a 70B variant, or something else (this materially affects GPU choice).
- Deployment preference: Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, or Private VPC/on-prem? You mentioned a leaning toward Dedicated with VPC peering for now — confirm.
- Security/compliance asks: procurement and security will send the questionnaire; we can include SOC2 artifacts and network details in our next packet.
- Timeline and procurement: when do you expect to finalize procurement/PO?

Suggested next steps:
1) FinLytics fills the worksheet and returns by EOD Wednesday (2026-09-01).
2) Redwood schedules a 60-minute sizing deep-dive (eng + infra) to walk numbers and recommend GPU SKUs. Proposed slots: Thu 2026-09-02 09:00–10:00 PT or Fri 2026-09-03 11:00–12:00 PT.
3) Redwood follows up with a draft Dedicated proposal (capacity + pricing + network diagram) within 3 business days after the deep-dive.

If helpful I can pre-populate a couple of rows in the worksheet with our assumptions so you can edit directly.

Thanks — Vivek

Hi Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers inline below and a few clarifying questions.

Traffic profile:
- Sustained: ~30 req/s (concurrent small user flows across our product).
- Peak bursts: up to 120 req/s for 2–5 minute windows during promotions.
- Average concurrency: typically 25–40 active sessions that can generate overlapping calls.

Token mix (per request):
- Input median: ~150 tokens.
- Output median: ~350 tokens.
- 95th percentile: ~1,200 tokens (long-form generation).

Latency goal: 95th <= 300–400ms for interactive features; for batch/async jobs we tolerate higher.

Model family: experimenting with a tuned Llama-2 family (65–70B) but we may test smaller quantized variants for cost. Will confirm exact checkpoint.

Deployment: We prefer Dedicated capacity in our cloud tenant with VPC peering — want customer-managed VPC peering for IP whitelisting. Private on-prem is not in scope for the POC but could be later. Hosted API is fine for quick experiments but not acceptable for production due to data residency rules.

Security: we'll send the questionnaire (attached) and expect SOC2 Type II evidence + network diagrams.

Procurement timeline: Procurement expects to review proposals this month; target PO in 4–6 weeks if pricing and SLAs align.

Would appreciate if you can give a ballpark recommendation on GPU SKU(s) for the profile above (latency vs throughput tradeoff) ahead of the deep-dive — even a 1‑line guideline helps.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver James
Head of ML Platform, FinLytics

Team — forwarding FinLytics' numbers (see Oliver's reply). Can you review and propose a short ballpark GPU recommendation and a list of clarifying datapoints we should ask FinLytics to fill in the worksheet before the deep-dive?

My high-level thoughts: given 95th up to 1,200 tokens and interactive latency target, they need a low-latency option but also must handle 120 req/s bursts. Tradeoffs:
- Option A (latency-focused): 2 x H100-80GB (or 4 x H100 depending on KV cache needs) tuned with quantization and smaller beam sizes can hit 95th ~300–400ms for a 65–70B Llama variant for modest concurrency, but cost is higher.
- Option B (throughput-focused): 6–8 x A100-80GB (sharded) provides better throughput and smoother handling of bursts if they can accept slightly higher p95 latency or use batching.

Clarifying asks to put in worksheet before call:
- Which exact checkpoint / tokenizer do they plan to use? (affects memory & KV cache)
- Burst shape: is 120 req/s sustained across 2–5 minutes or multiple overlapping bursts?
- Do they expect many long-context queries simultaneously (multi-thousand token contexts)?
- Will they want persistent KV cache across sessions?

I can draft these into the worksheet and send back to Oliver. Priyom/Karthik — any immediate changes or numbers you want to include in ballpark recs?

— Vivek

Adding engineering notes and a short recommendation to share with the customer. I kept it high level so procurement has something to react to quickly.

Engineering observations / recommendations (quick):
- Given token mix and 120 req/s burst shape, plan for headroom: target sustained effective throughput of 40–50 req/s and burst headroom to 120. We size for the sustained baseline + ~2x burst buffer.
- Model assumption: 65–70B Llama-variant, FP16 or 4-bit quantized. If they choose smaller 13–33B variants we can reduce GPU count significantly.
- GPU guidance (ballpark):
  * Latency-optimized: 3 x H100-80GB (recommended start) — lower p95 for interactive use, supports larger context and KV cache, simpler single-node behavior for dev.
  * Throughput-optimized: 6 x A100-80GB (or 4x A100 + dynamic autoscale) — better sustained token throughput per-dollar, more complex sharding.
- Memory/KV: For 1,200-token tails and persistent cache, plan additional memory reservation (approx +20% to model memory budget).
- Networking: VPC peering with static IPs; recommend private peering and route filters.
- Compliance: we can provide SOC2 Type II report and architecture diagram in the proposal packet.

Proposed next steps (to share with customer):
1) FinLytics fills our two highlighted rows in the worksheet (burst pattern detail + exact model checkpoint).
2) Sizing deep-dive: Tue 2026-09-07 09:00–10:00 PT or Wed 2026-09-08 16:00–17:00 PT — please confirm a slot.
3) Redwood delivers a draft Dedicated capacity offer (SKU, network, estimate pricing) within 72 hours after deep-dive.

I'll create a short slide with the two SKU options and expected monthly cost ranges to help procurement. Vivek — do you want me to attach that before the deep-dive?

— Marissa
